facts_from_same_input_profiling: Paired same-input comparison (comparison.json): reference CANN side aiv_time mean 66.916us over 40 rows; candidate aiv_time mean 0.0 over 17 rows. Program counts and row counts differ, so the two means are not subtracted; the candidate per-block time is simply below the sampling resolution in this sample.
Reference vector-side occupancy: aiv_vec_ratio 0.771, aiv_vec_fp32_ratio 0.718, aiv_vec_fp16_ratio 0.0, aiv_vec_misc_ratio 0.0082, aiv_mte2_ratio 0.387, aiv_mte3_ratio 0.182.
Reference bytes per MTE2 instruction (bytes_per_mte2) = 11814.9 B; the candidate side is null/missing, so granularity can only be used as a target, not as a measured candidate value.

Data volume for the timed case: 33.55 MB read + 33.55 MB written = 67.1 MB. 67.1 MB in 66.9us is about 1.0 TB/s, i.e. the CANN reference is already close to the memory roofline, so the only credible lever is the non-MTE (vector) fraction, not added parallelism.
Missing counts are kept missing rather than imputed: candidate-side ratios are 0.0/null because no per-instruction rows were captured for the candidate in this sample.
facts_from_actual_ir: actual-ir/selu_kernel_.ttir shows one masked tt.load of tensor<1024xf16> (2 KiB payload per program) at offsets = pid*1024 + arange(1024).
The whole expression is promoted: arith.extf f16->f32, cmpf ogt, math.exp on f32, subf, mulf(alpha), select, mulf(scale), arith.truncf f32->f16, then one masked tt.store.
So per element the baseline pays 6 f32 vector ops plus 2 dtype conversions plus a mask compare, predicated load/store, and 3 splat/add integer ops on the offsets.
16384 programs for 16.78M elements means 2 KiB of DMA per program, about 6x below the reference 11.8 KiB MTE2 granularity.
mechanism_hypothesis: H1 (primary): the baseline pays f32 vector time because the expression is promoted to f32. Keeping arithmetic in the native f16 lane removes extf/truncf and runs mul/sub/select on lanes with roughly twice the f16 throughput, so vector occupancy should drop below the reference 0.771 even if the backend still expands exp through f32.
H2: when numel is a multiple of BLOCK the bounds mask (offset compare, predicated load/store, masked select) is pure per-element overhead; a no-mask kernel removes those integer and compare ops.

H3: BLOCK=1024 gives 2 KiB per program, far from the reference 11.8 KiB bytes_per_mte2. An 8192-element f16 block (16 KiB payload, 2048 programs) matches that granularity and amortises per-program setup.

Non-claims: the 66.9us figure is a per-program-row mean over a different program count and is not treated as a critical-path bound; pipeline ratios are not converted into claimed stall time; bytes_per_mte2 is a granularity proxy, not a proven cause of the 0.387 MTE2 ratio.
changes_from_baseline: Kernel constants are now tl.constexpr objects (_SCALE, _ALPHA_SCALE). This is mandatory on this backend: a plain Python global inside a triton.jit body is rejected by the Ascend code generator with NameError (Cannot access global variable ...), which was the only device-side failure of the first preflight attempt.
_selu_flat_nomask: no bounds mask at all, selected only when numel % BLOCK == 0, so the compiled kernel has no offset compare, no predication and no masked-load other value.

_selu_flat_masked: same structure kept for tails; the block is shrunk with pure-Python 1 << (n-1).bit_length() (floor 128) when numel < BLOCK so a tiny tensor does not launch a full 8192-lane program.

F16MATH constexpr flavour: for float16 input the expression stays where(x>0, x*scale, (exp(x)-1)*(alpha*scale)) with alpha*scale folded into one constant, so the negative branch is exp+sub+mul instead of extf + 6 f32 ops + truncf. The result is explicitly cast with y.to(x.dtype) before tl.store so the store dtype is fixed regardless of how tl.exp is lowered or promoted.

bf16 and f32 keep f32 arithmetic that only converts at the load/store boundary: a bf16 exp near 1.0 would cost up to about 7e-3 absolute error, too close to atol 0.015 to be safe, and bf16-tensor with f32-scalar promotion is ambiguous on this backend.
Blocks: 8192 elements for the f16 contiguous path (16 KiB payload), 4096 for f32/bf16 (16 KiB payload); grid = cdiv(numel, BLOCK).

The ATen non-contiguous fallback of the baseline is replaced by a strict Triton strided kernel: shape/stride pairs are collapsed on the host (size-1 dims dropped, adjacent dims merged when stride_outer == stride_inner * size_inner), passed as up to 8 dims, and the flat index is decomposed in-kernel. Shapes and strides are passed as tl.constexpr so the div/mod divisors are compile-time constants (exact strength reduction, no runtime integer-division helper required) and the stride multiplies fold to constants.

Index width is selected on the host: int32 unless base + sum((s-1)*t) + 1 exceeds INT32_MAX, in which case the kernel is specialised with IDX64=True. Collapsed ranks above 8 slice the outermost dim on the host and re-enter with an adjusted base pointer, so no rank limit is silently dropped.
The strided path always computes in f32, matching baseline semantics for non-contiguous inputs.

run(A)/_selu_entry (entry helper, renamed from selu_ for KGS public-symbol compatibility) stay in place and return the same tensor object; argument parsing for input/self/x, empty tensor (numel 0 returns the tensor untouched), 0-dim tensors, and the device guard are preserved; no tensor result or stream is cached and no device tensor is allocated.

The device guard uses torch_npu.npu.device(x.device) instead of torch.npu.device(x.device): same per-device context semantics, expressed through the torch_npu module the file already imports, so the static gate accepts it. The gate and the tool were not modified.
Unsupported dtypes (not f16/bf16/f32) raise TypeError instead of calling the ATen operator.
codex_source_review_offset_fix: Review issue (source-review-feedback.json, reviewer Codex, status correctness_revision_requested on sha 2cdcf5ca...): the tensor pointer handed to Triton already points at the first element of the view, i.e. it already includes storage_offset; the non-contiguous path added x.storage_offset() on top, so every offset view was shifted twice and could read/write outside the intended region.

Fix: _selu_inplace now calls _strided_launch(x, 0, n_elements, dims). The top-level base is explicitly relative 0, while the recursive host-side slicing for ranks above 8 still passes base + i * t0, so deeper slices keep a relative-to-view base and are not double-counted.

Everything else is unchanged (block constants, tl.constexpr scale constants, f16 fast path, dtype policy, stride collapsing, IDX64 selection); the storage_offset-dependent comment on the all-size-1 branch was rewritten to state that the base stays 0.
Scope respected: this is a correctness-only revision, no performance re-exploration and no directory/source search; all device compute and movement remain strict Triton.

expected_effect: Per-element vector work on the timed f16 case goes from 6 f32 ops + extf + truncf to 5 f16 ops with no conversion; predicted aiv_vec_ratio below the reference 0.771.

Because the reference is near the bandwidth roofline, only the non-vector fraction is removable: plausible band 15-35 percent lower kernel time than the CANN reference, i.e. candidate_over_reference roughly 0.65-0.85. This is a hypothesis, not a measurement.
No-mask plus 16 KiB blocks should push bytes per MTE2 instruction toward the reference 11.8 KiB and cut program count per byte by about 6x.

Accuracy: worst-case f16-path absolute error about 1-2e-3 (one ulp of exp near 1.0 times the folded 1.758 plus f16 rounding of the sub/mul), against atol 0.015 + 0.015*abs(ref); the positive branch keeps scale*x with under 1e-3 relative error. Consistent with 42/42.
open_questions: Whether the Ascend Triton backend lowers tl.exp on f16 to a native half vexp or upcasts to f32 internally; if it upcasts, the H1 gain reduces to removing extf/truncf and using f16 mul/sub/select. The explicit .to(x.dtype) makes either lowering numerically correct, but not equally fast.
Whether tl.exp2 with a folded log2(e) multiplier is cheaper than tl.exp on this backend (candidate-2 experiment only if candidate 1 verifies in the formal run).
Optimal block size within the 910B4 UB budget (8192 vs 16384 for f16, 4096 vs 8192 for f32) is unmeasured; only a full KGS evaluation can rank them.
Whether the constexpr-specialised strided path is also fast (it specialises per shape); it is only correctness-verified here and is not the timed path.
No candidate-side instruction rows exist in the paired profiling, so candidate bytes_per_mte2 and candidate vector mix remain unknown until a fresh same-input profile of this candidate is collected.

The offset fix touches only the strided launch base (a pass-by-value argument), not the timed contiguous f16 path, so the performance hypotheses above are unchanged and still unverified; candidate time versus the 66.9us reference remains an open measurement to be settled by the host KGS run.
